title: Beef pies with a shortcrust shell
steps: Soften the onion in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes, then add the beef and brown it, breaking up lumps.
Stir in the 2 tbsp flour and tomato paste, then add the stock. Simmer for 20 minutes until thick and glossy. Season well and cool completely.
Rub the butter into the 350 g flour and a pinch of salt until it looks like breadcrumbs. Add the iced water a little at a time and bring together into a dough. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line four individual pie tins about 10 cm across. Roll the rest for lids.
Fill the cases with the cooled meat, brush the rims with egg, press the lids on and trim. Cut a small steam hole in each and brush the tops with egg.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden. Rest for 5 minutes and serve with tomato sauce.
notes: Cooling the filling first stops the pastry going soggy. Bought puff pastry makes a good lid.

title: Chocolate and coconut lamingtons
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C and line a 20 by 30 cm tin with baking paper.
Whisk the eggs and sugar for 8 to 10 minutes until thick, pale and tripled in volume.
Sift the flour and baking powder over the eggs and fold in gently. Fold in the melted butter and milk.
Pour into the tin and bake for 22 to 25 minutes until springy. Cool, wrap, and leave overnight if you can; a firm sponge is easier to ice.
Cut into 16 squares. Sift the icing sugar and cocoa into a bowl, add the butter and hot milk and stir until smooth and fairly thin.
Dip each square in the icing using two forks, let the excess drip off, then roll in coconut. Rest on a rack until set.
notes: Keep the icing warm over a bowl of hot water so it stays runny.

title: Chewy Anzac biscuits
steps: Heat the oven to 160 C and line two trays with baking paper.
Mix the oats, flour, sugar and coconut in a large bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together over low heat. Stir the baking soda into the boiling water and add it to the pan; it will foam.
Pour the butter mixture into the dry ingredients and stir to a crumbly dough.
Roll tablespoons of dough into balls, place 5 cm apart on the trays and flatten slightly.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until golden. Cool on the trays; they firm as they cool.
notes: Bake 3 minutes less for chewy biscuits and 3 minutes more for crisp ones.

title: Oven-baked damper
steps: Heat the oven to 210 C and dust a tray with flour.
Mix the flour, baking powder and salt, then rub in the butter until crumbly.
Add most of the milk and mix with a knife to a soft dough, adding more milk only if needed. Do not overwork it.
Shape into a round about 4 cm thick, score a cross on top and place on the tray.
Bake for 28 to 32 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath. Eat warm with butter and golden syrup.
notes: Over a campfire, bake it in a lidded cast-iron pot buried in coals.

title: Sausage sizzle with onions
steps: Heat a barbecue flat plate or heavy frying pan over medium heat and oil it lightly.
Cook the onions on the plate for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden. Push them to the side.
Cook the sausages for 12 to 15 minutes, turning often, until browned and cooked through with no pink inside.
Lay a slice of bread flat, add a sausage and some onions, squeeze on sauce, and fold the bread around it.

title: Pan-seared barramundi with lemon myrtle butter

ingredients.note: ground, or use 2 tsp lemon zest

steps: Mix the softened butter with half the lemon myrtle and a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Pat the fillets very dry, season with salt and rub with the remaining lemon myrtle.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Lay the fillets skin side down and press gently for 10 seconds.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the skin is crisp and the flesh is opaque most of the way up, then turn for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the butter and lime juice to the pan, spoon over the fish as it melts, and serve straight away.

title: Seared kangaroo with red wine sauce
steps: Rub the fillet with half the oil, salt and pepper.
Heat the remaining oil in a heavy pan over high heat until almost smoking. Sear the fillet for 2 to 3 minutes per side for medium-rare; do not cook past medium or it will turn tough.
Remove to a warm plate, cover loosely, and rest for 8 minutes.
In the same pan, soften the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the wine and stock. Boil until reduced by half, scraping up the browned bits.
Off the heat, swirl in the cold butter. Slice the kangaroo across the grain and spoon over the sauce.

title: Vegemite on buttered toast
steps: Toast the bread until golden.
Spread the butter on while the toast is hot so it melts in.
Scrape a very thin layer of Vegemite over the top, cut into fingers or triangles and eat at once.
notes: Use a small amount; the flavour is very strong. Avocado or sliced cheese are common additions.

title: Oysters natural with vinegar dressing
steps: Keep the oysters on ice until you shuck them. Discard any that are open and do not close, or smell off.
Hold an oyster in a folded cloth, hinge towards you. Work the tip of a short oyster knife into the hinge, twist to pop it, and slide the blade along the top shell to cut the muscle.
Lift off the top shell and loosen the oyster from the bottom shell without spilling the liquor.
Mix the vinegar, onion and a little pepper. Serve the oysters on crushed ice with lemon wedges and the dressing.
notes: Buy from a trusted supplier and eat shortly after opening. Pregnant people, and those with weakened immunity, should avoid raw shellfish.

title: Pie floater with pea soup

ingredients.note: hot, baked (see the Australian meat pie recipe)

steps: Put the peas, onion, carrot and stock in a large pot and bring to the boil. Skim any foam.
Simmer, partly covered, for 60 minutes, stirring now and then, until the peas collapse into a thick soup.
Season, then stir or lightly blend until mostly smooth. Add a splash of water if too thick.
Ladle soup into four wide bowls. Set a hot pie in the centre of each, top with tomato sauce, and serve.
